Subject: Q3 retainer invoice - split between US & EU entities + VAT question

Hi Monica,

Hope you	're well. Finance is preparing the Q3 retainer invoice and we'd like to split the invoice lines between our US entity (Acme Health USA, TaxID: 12-3456789) and our EU subsidiary (Acme Health EU, VAT: EU987654321) according to the product/services consumption outlined in the attached usage export.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood issue a single PDF that lists the two legal entities as separate bill-to lines (so our AP can route payments to two bank accounts)?
- For VAT: we	're not sure whether the EU portion should be reverse-charged or if Redwood needs to charge VAT on that line. Acme EU is registered and will provide VAT registration if needed. If you need a VAT declaration from Redwood, can you confirm which entity will own VAT on the EU line?

Also need PO: ACME-Q3-RET-001 to appear on both line items. Ideally we'd receive a mutual action plan for remittance and timing for collection.

Thanks,

Hi Liam,

Thanks for the details and the usage export. Quick confirmation: we can produce a single PDF invoice that shows two bill-to sections and two remittance instructions. A couple of operational clarifications from our side so we can send a clean MOP (mutual action plan):

- Which amounts should flow to Acme Health USA vs Acme Health EU? The CSV helps but can you confirm the allocation percentage per product line (or a simple mapping)?
- For the EU leg, please attach Acme Health EU VAT registration document so our tax team can validate reverse-charge eligibility.
- Do you require separate GL/PO mapping per line? You mentioned PO ACME-Q3-RET-001 should appear on both lines — we can include the same PO but map to different GL codes if you provide them.

I'm attaching a proposed-split-matrix.csv that mirrors how we usually structure multi-entity invoices. Ben, Kimberly - looped in for approval of routing and GST/VAT ownership.

Next steps: once we have your confirmed split and VAT reg, Redwood will:
1) Confirm which Redwood legal entity will recognize revenue for each line and whether VAT must be charged or if reverse-charge applies.
2) Produce draft combined invoice PDF and remittance page.
3) Share DocuSign link for any signature (if required) and post invoice to payment portal.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Manager, Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Monica / Kim,

Reviewed the proposed-split-matrix. My recommendations:
- Revenue recognition: Redwood US (Redwood Inc., EIN: 98-7654321) should book the US lines. For EU lines, we should assess whether Redwood EU (Redwood Ltd., VAT: GB123456789) will book revenue or if we treat it as cross-border and keep revenue in Redwood US with VAT reversal. Our tax team prefers to keep revenue where the contract was signed unless there's a significant transfer of risk.
- VAT: If Acme EU provides valid VAT reg and the place of supply is B2B in the EU, we should apply reverse-charge (no VAT charged by Redwood), and include a VAT note on the invoice.
- GL codes: Kimberly, please confirm GL mapping for the two destination accounts (product/service GL vs support GL). We need GL codes to populate the CSV and the invoice line memo.

Happy to quick-call with Liam if that speeds confirmation.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference
